abstract: For any given uncountable cardinal $\kappa$, we show that every $\kappa$-edge-connected graph admits a minor embedding of the graph $T_{\kappa}\star1$ (the $\kappa$-regular tree with a new apex vertex adjacent to all its nodes), which is itself $\kappa$-edge-connected. This extends a previous result of Kurkofka regarding unavoidable minors of $\aleph_0$-edge-connected graphs to all uncountable cardinalities $\kappa$.
hook: Every graph with uncountable edge-connectivity kappa contains a kappa-connected tree-plus-apex minor.
summary: A highly connected infinite graph must contain a specific connected pattern: a regular tree with one extra vertex joined to every node. The authors prove this for every uncountable cardinal kappa, extending a known result for the countable case. It is a pure existence proof for infinite graphs, with no construction for finite settings.
title: The unavoidable minor in graphs of uncountable edge-connectivity
